scope: Lab-only asset selection, safe Action Lab handoff and beginner workflow guidance.
sourcePolicy: Only the newly supplied 3d-lab(8).zip was used as application source. No older application or cApp source was merged.
changes: Searchable, filterable and paginated Action Lab asset chooser, with direct GLB import.
Assets right-click, ellipsis and keyboard menus plus inspector Open/Continue in Action Lab.
Persistent model identity and human, animal or mechanical setup guidance based on actual rig, bindings and keyed actions.
Save/Discard/Cancel switching, same-source session continuation and transactional failure recovery.
Detached import validation, incompatible bind-pose and unsupported mixed animation rejection.
Busy/candidate and async-load safeguards, contained dialog focus and mobile/fullscreen access.
preserved: Original assets and source GLB bytes/metadata.
Saved Action Lab recipes, joints, bindings, constraints, clip keys and source provenance.
Existing Local AI 0.21.0 / MCP 0.24.20 setup and neural-model integrations.

checks: Action Lab exposes asset choice and import with beginner guidance on first visit
Import from Action Lab saves a real GLB and opens it directly for rigging
Asset browser searches names, folder, tags and notes; filters and selection are explicit
Larger collections paginate and name sorting remains predictable
Right click, ellipsis and keyboard menus all offer direct Action Lab handoff
Maximum-length asset titles open without overflowing the editable title limit
Same-source reopening retains unsaved rig changes and Undo history
Switch Cancel preserves the complete document and keeps the picker available
Switch Discard is explicit and loads the chosen static mesh without old joints
Save and switch stores the rig, weights and named keys as a separate action asset
Reopen action draft restores all rig, binding, constraint and clip data
The first async asset switch owns the request and prevents overlapping user switches
Immediate workspace return cancels stale static previews and retains the open action session
An imported animated GLB keeps the embedded rig, skin weights and keys
Failed Save and switch leaves current work intact and permits cancellation
Malformed import is rejected before replacing or saving current edits
A valid GLB with unsupported morph geometry is decoded and rejected without scene loss
An incompatible imported bind pose is rejected without corrupting the current rig
A removed asset fails safely without losing the edited scene
Asset names are rendered as text, and picker keyboard focus stays within its dialog
Asset replacement is blocked during an owned model operation and skeleton review
Mobile and fullscreen retain accessible asset picking without horizontal overflow
Saved action persists through real reload and reopens without an AI model
Asset handoffs preserve the original static GLB bytes and metadata
No uncaught browser errors or unexpected network access
browser.scope: Built Lab, real browser IndexedDB and GLB parser/exporter. Controlled animation bridge tests only busy/candidate UX, not inference.

visualReview: Desktop Action Lab and 390px mobile picker screenshots inspected; source identity, guide and selection remain readable, with scrolling for narrow dialogs.
limits: Browser execution used Linux Chromium, real IndexedDB and GLB parsing/export; Windows/WebView2 was not run.
A controlled animation bridge exercised only busy and candidate safeguards, not model inference.
No new neural-quality or RTX 4070/CUDA acceptance claim; 0.8.0 inference records remain historical.
Imports require supported self-contained skeletal/static GLBs. Morph targets, object-only motion and incompatible bind poses are rejected with feedback.
Setup guidance describes scene structure; users must still inspect joint placement, weights, contacts and movement.
